MANAGEMENT OF NSTEMI/NOMI 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The HEART Score for Chest Pain in the ED 
History 
* Highly suspicious 
* 2 points 
* Moderately suspicious 
* 1 point 
* Slightly / non-suspicious 
* 0 points 
ECG 
* Significant ST depression 
* 2 points 
* Nonspecific repolarisation 
* 1 point 
* Normal 
* 0 points 
Age 
* ≥ 65 years 
* 2 points 
* > 45 - < 65 years 
* 1 point 
* ≤ 45 years 
* 0 points 
Risk Factors 
* ≥ 3 risk factors 
* 2 points 
* 1 or 2 risk factors 
* 1 point 
* No risk factors 
* 0 points 
Troponin 
* ≥ 3 x normal limit 
* 2 points 
* > 1 - < 3 x normal limit 
* 1 point 
* ≤ normal limit 
* 0 points 
Risk Factors: Diabetes Mellitus, current or recent (<1 month) smoker, 
Hypertension, Hypercholestrolaemia, Family History, Obesity 
Score 0 - 3 (low risk) 
2.5% MACE over next 6 weeks 
Score 4 - 6 (intermediate risk) 
20.3% MACE over next 6 weeks 
Score 7 - 10 (high risk) 
72.7% MACE over next 6 weeks 
MACE = Major Adverse Cardiac Event 
 
NSTE - ACS 
High Risk Unstable Angina (UA) / NSTEMI 
Delta troponin (rising & falling) =  NSTEMI/NOMI 
ST depression ≥ 0.5mm (see box for criteria) 
ST elevation > 0.5mm but < 1mm 
Dynamic inverted t-waves 
i.e. T-waves previously been upright but are inverted 
when the patient has chest pain
